items.question: How can an embodied and divided deity be invoked and act effectively?
premises: Meditation and worship take diverse forms.
An embodied and divided deity can be invoked.
Such invocation can produce effective action in an instant.
items.inference: The variety of meditation and worship is effective because an embodied, divided deity can be invoked and act immediately.
items.plain_english: Thus the variety of meditation, worship, and the like becomes effective in action: an embodied, divided deity, when invoked, can abandon its own enjoyments and act in an instant.

items.question: Does the claim that a god comes and acts fit the true nature of reality?
premises: The report that a god comes and acts may suit scriptural statements.
The ultimate nature is formless and beyond such limitations.
A doctrine must fit that ultimate nature to be fully valid.
items.inference: The coming-and-going account is only scripturally suitable, while the formless nature is what truly fits.
items.plain_english: Saying 'O god, he comes' is fitting only within scriptural statements; but all this is truly fitting only as the nature of the formless and so forth.

items.question: What is the true source of the appearance of division?
premises: The self alone has that ultimate nature.
The self appears in divided forms.
This appearing as division is the very nature of consciousness.
items.inference: Division is not external to the self but is consciousness manifesting according to its own nature.
items.plain_english: Indeed the self alone, being of that nature, appears just so through division; for this is the very nature of consciousness, and that alone is what appears.

items.question: When is karmic differentiation treated as an impurity and when is it not?
premises: Scripture defines karmic impurity as being seized by division.
Initiation and ritual action operate within differentiated forms.
In the context of initiation, that differentiation is not treated as impurity.
items.inference: Karmic division counts as impurity in bondage but not in the liberating use of initiation and ritual.
items.plain_english: In scripture the karmic impurity is defined as being seized by division; but in the practice of initiation and related rites, it is not regarded as an impurity.

compound describing initiation as true awareness itself

items.question: What is initiation in its essential nature?
premises: Initiation is directed toward burning away the whole division-made world of transmigration.
Its true function is not merely external ritual.
In reality it consists in true consciousness of that liberating kind.
items.inference: Initiation is essentially the true consciousness that destroys division-based transmigration.
items.plain_english: For initiation is vowed to burning away the entire world of transmigration made of division; and in reality it is of the nature of that true consciousness.

rows.grounds: fused connective and locative referring to the highest teaching
in the discipline of direct knowledge

items.question: What is realized when the domain of division is pacified in the supreme teaching?
premises: The supreme teaching states that one who knows thus knows in truth.
This knowledge arises in the yoga of realization.
In that yoga the sphere of division becomes quieted.
items.inference: True knowledge in the supreme doctrine consists in realization when division is pacified.
items.plain_english: Thus it is said in the supreme doctrine: one who knows in this way knows in truth; for in the yoga of realization, when the sphere of division is quieted, this is understood.

items.question: If the self is one with Śiva, what meaning do bondage and liberation have?
premises: In realization the self alone is Śiva, the one reality.
From that standpoint bondage and liberation lose their ultimate distinction.
Teaching still speaks of initiation to lead one into that great consciousness.
items.inference: Bondage and liberation are pedagogical distinctions used to guide entry into the nondual consciousness where self is Śiva.
items.plain_english: The self alone is Śiva, the one reality—so what bondage is there, and what liberation? Yet this is taught for the sake of entry into the great consciousness of initiation.

rows.grounds: fused compound referring to initiation characterized by ritual action
compound locative plural describing karmic actions governed by inherent necessity

items.question: How does action-based initiation remove karmic and other impurities?
premises: There is an initiation whose nature is action.
Its purpose is the removal of karmic and other impurities.
It operates within actions compelled by a fixed force fashioned by nature.
items.inference: Action-based initiation works by transforming karmic actions that are otherwise governed by fixed necessity.
items.plain_english: This initiation, whose nature is action, is for the removal of karmic and other impurities, operating within actions that are driven by the fixed force fashioned by nature.

rows.grounds: compound naming limiting determinations along the paths of space, limited agency, and time

items.question: How can the fruition of karma be experienced simultaneously through initiation?
premises: Initiation can bring about the experience of karma for the initiate.
This fruition can occur simultaneously through mantra power.
The limiting determinations of breath, space, limited agency, and time are thereby engaged.
items.inference: Mantra power in initiation can compress and resolve karmic fruition across the usual limiting paths.
uncertainties: The exact scope of deśakalākālādhvaniścayāḥ is compressed in the compound and follows traditional Trika categories.
items.plain_english: Because his experience is brought about simultaneously through the power of mantra, the determinations belonging to breath, space, limited agency, and time are likewise brought into play.

rows.grounds: compound indicating the full range of levels

items.question: Across what range are the initiate's births and experiences unfolded?
premises: The initiate's births are unfolded across the whole cosmic range.
That range extends from earth up to Śiva.
Within that range occur birth, experience, authority, and dissolution.
items.inference: Initiatory transformation encompasses the full spectrum of existence from the lowest to the highest level.
items.plain_english: His births are unfolded from earth all the way up to Śiva, and right there he becomes subject to birth, experience, authority, and dissolution.

items.question: How does initiation block all prior karmic powers between guru and disciple?
premises: The initiate is elevated from one level and established in another.
Guru and disciple meet in a state grounded in settled consciousness and free of karmic mind.
Initiation operates through a non-conceptual transmission between them.
items.inference: Mutual non-conceptual initiation between guru and disciple restrains all prior karmic powers.
uncertainties: niṣkarmacetor is metrically compressed; taken as a genitive dual/collective sense in context.
items.plain_english: Thus, having been arranged and elevated from one level and placed in another, initiation—through the mutual, non-conceptual meeting of a guru established in settled consciousness and a disciple of actionless mind—blocks all the powers of prior karma.

items.question: Do external Śaiva ritual forms fully eliminate the obscurity of division?
premises: Śaiva ritual employs substances like rice, sesame, ghee, and oblations.
These forms are fashioned according to Śaiva necessity and operate at a clear level.
Even so, division continues to operate.
items.inference: External ritual forms do not completely uproot the obscurity of division because differentiation still persists.
uncertainties: niśāprapañco is metaphorical; interpreted as the expanse of obscurity rather than literal night.
items.plain_english: Even there, the series of rice, sesame, ghee, oblations, and so forth—fashioned according to Śaiva necessity—does not, even at a clear stage, make the expanse of obscurity rootless, because division still continues to operate.
